item.title: Xi orders all-out rescue work in Xizang
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-24
Xi orders all-out rescue work in Xizang Efforts urged to prevent secondary disasters after powerful quake President Xi Jinping has urged all-out search and rescue efforts for the missing and prompt medical treatment for the injured, in order to minimize casualties after a magnitude 7 earthquake rocked Drachen county in Nagchu, Southwest China's Xizang autonomous region. The quake, which struck at 10:33 pm on Thursday at a depth of 10 kilometers, killed 16 people, injured at least 76, and damaged or flattened 339 houses, with search for survivors continuing on Friday. In an instruction issued on Friday morning, Xi noted that the affected county is at a high altitude with low temperatures, emphasizing the need to closely monitor seismic activity and weather conditions to prevent secondary disasters. It is imperative to dispatch emergency rescue supplies, properly accommodate the affected residents, and repair damaged infrastructure as quickly as possible to safeguard people's lives and property, Xi said. In a separate instruction, Premier Li Qiang called for swift assessment of the situation. Given the county's high altitude and the frequent aftershocks, Li urged the Ministry of Emergency Management and the China Earthquake Administration, together with relevant authorities, to strengthen seismic monitoring and forecasting, and step up disaster prevention and response efforts.

item.title: Citizens' role in judicial cases grows
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-24
Citizens' role in judicial cases grows Ordinary Chinese citizens are playing a growing role in judicial proceedings, particularly in cases involving public interest or significant social impact, by serving as people's assessors and offering their perspectives, an official with China's top court said on Friday. Sun Zhenping, head of the Political Department of the Supreme People's Court, said people's assessors help promote justice and enhance public security under the rule of law. Their participation also reflects the concept of whole-process people's democracy, he said. China's people's assessor system, which dates back to the 1930s, allows citizens aged 28 or older to participate directly in the judicial proceedings. The system safeguards the public's rights to be informed, participate in, express opinions and oversee judicial activities. In April 2018, a law regulating the selection, duties and conduct of assessors was adopted and took effect immediately. "Following the law, assessors are increasingly involved in cases of public interest or broad concern, such as those related to public safety, the national economy, people's livelihood, and public morals," Sun said. For public interest litigation cases, in which defendants face possible prison sentences of 10 years or more, life imprisonment or death penalty, and disputes with significant social impact — including those involving land expropriation, environmental protection, and food and drug safety — the law requires a seven-member collegial panel of judges and assessors, he said. "These efforts highlight the growing depth and breadth of assessor involvement in our judicial proceedings," he added. Li Wenyun, a people's assessor who works on a community committee in Beijing's Haidian district, shared her experience handling a case in which a man surnamed Mu mentally abused his former girlfriend, leading to her suicide. Mu was ultimately sentenced to three years and two months in prison for maltreatment. Li recalled that before the hearing, she carefully reviewed the case files and checked the evidence item by item, focusing on where Mu and the victim had lived together, how often and for how long they had cohabited, and their financial dealings. "That allowed me to ask Mu targeted questions during the hearing, helping the collegial panel piece together the facts," she said. "I started from the simple principle that men and women should treat each other with respect and care, and drew on my experience working in the residential area to offer my views on whether Mu's conduct constituted the crime of maltreatment and whether it was linked to the victim's suicide. The panel adopted my opinions," she said. After the trial, Li also offered suggestions on the findings of fact and drafting legal explanations. "What I did was to make the judgment strictly follow the law while better responding to public concerns," she added. She said participating in case handling is both a duty and an opportunity to learn about the law, helping raise legal awareness among more residents. Ning Liping, a people's assessor in Sichuan province and a university teacher, has drawn on her expertise in environmental protection cases. In one case, she identified flaws in an appraisal report, helping the panel avoid delays and suggesting more feasible restoration methods. While expressing pride in participating in judicial work, Ning said, "Being an assessor has also enriched my research and teaching, as real-world cases can provide valuable study samples and lively teaching materials, taking my teaching beyond textbook theory." Shi Dongbo, another official with the SPC's Political Department, praised assessors' contributions but stressed the importance of effective judicial guidance. The SPC has issued clear guidelines requiring judges to brief assessors on case facts, disputes and court procedures before hearings, ensuring they have access to case files and understand the rules for questioning during trials, Shi said. By the end of 2025, China had about 340,000 people's assessors, nearly three times the number in 2013, according to data released by the SPC in January.

item.title: China's snow leopard population doubles
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-24
China's snow leopard population doubles China's snow leopard population has doubled to about 5,000 since systematic conservation efforts began in 2013, with the species' habitat expanding to approximately 2.08 million square kilometers, the National Forestry and Grassland Administration said on Thursday. The figure means China now accounts for more than 60 percent of the global snow leopard habitat, the administration said in a media release on Friday, which coincided with the International Snow Leopard Day. China is also home to the world's largest snow leopard distribution area and the biggest population of the species, the release said. Known as the "king of the mountains", the snow leopard is a national first-class protected animal, as well as a flagship and umbrella species of high-altitude ecosystems. Its presence is considered an important indicator of the integrity, stability and health of alpine ecosystems. China has continued to strengthen its protected area system in the species' core distribution areas. Two national parks and 78 other important protected areas have been established in key habitats, while more than 800,000 sq km of snow leopard habitat has been placed under strict protection. Nearly 40 percent of the species' potential habitat is now under standardized management, the administration said. The country has also made progress in rebuilding populations in areas where snow leopards had disappeared. In the Helan Mountains, where snow leopards had become locally extinct, China launched its first systematic snow leopard reintroduction pilot project. The program has included individual selection, health assessments, genetic testing, acclimatization training, release and long-term monitoring. Eight snow leopards have so far been introduced into the mountains. Together with individuals that arrived through natural dispersal, some snow leopards have established stable home ranges and begun hunting independently. In 2026, the project achieved what the administration described as a complete conservation cycle: release, establishment in the wild, natural pairing, birth in the wild and successful rearing of a cub. The achievement is considered a major breakthrough in global snow leopard reintroduction and has filled a long-standing gap in the breeding history of wild snow leopards in the Helan Mountains. Shi Kun, chief expert on snow leopards at the Feline Research Center of the National Forestry and Grassland Administration, said a camera this year captured an adult snow leopard with a cub in the Helan Mountains. Through individual identification, researchers determined that the female was one released in 2024, he said. They estimate that the cub was born in the spring of 2025. Despite the progress, conservation still faces challenges from climate change, habitat fragmentation and human-wildlife conflict. Shi said global warming could reduce snow cover and make areas that were previously difficult to access available for grazing. Livestock can become prey, creating a greater risk of conflict. Snow leopards are also dependent on high-altitude habitats with relatively little human disturbance, Shi said. A clearer picture of the species' distribution is another priority. Researchers need to identify core habitats and movement corridors, while assessing how roads, infrastructure and major settlements divide and fragment those areas, Shi said. The administration said China will continue to improve its legal and policy framework, expand scientific monitoring and promote community participation. houliqiang@chinadaily.com.cn

item.title: Resolution 2758 a pillar for Global South cooperation
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-24
Resolution 2758 a pillar for Global South cooperation This year marks the 55th anniversary of the United Nations General Assembly Resolution 2758, a pivotal milestone that made the one-China principle a fundamental norm governing international relations and a broad consensus of the international community. This landmark achievement has significantly enhanced China's engagement in UN affairs, thereby amplifying the voice and influence of developing nations. The adoption of the resolution highlights the interplay of shifting global power dynamics, coordination among UN members, and multilateral institutional processes, and is a historical reference for collective action by the Global South today. The current cooperation among Global South countries on development reflects their growing ability to engage in international affairs. This progress is supported by the representation and consultation channels provided by international institutions, and by sustained economic and social development and collective action. Despite differences, these countries share common concerns in development financing, trade opportunities, technology access, and representation in international bodies. Collaboration with China enhances local development and global governance, strengthening their influence through institution building and international discourse. Trade cooperation underscores deep economic ties, with South-South trade reaching $7.2 trillion in 2025, accounting for 28 percent of total global goods trade. China's vast market, comprehensive manufacturing system, and supply chain linkages offer developing countries access to industrial goods, production means and market opportunities. As cooperation deepens, these trade relationships are poised to enhance export diversification, industrial upgrading, and value-added growth. The Belt and Road Initiative enhances transport, energy supply and information connectivity for participating countries. By integrating infrastructure development with industrial ecosystems, operations, maintenance, and talent training, the benefits extend beyond projects to include business operations, job creation, and regional economic linkages, transforming connectivity into local development capacity. Cooperation in public health and food security has bolstered development resilience, evolving from emergency support to technical collaboration and capacity building. Additionally, partnerships in green energy, climate adaptation, and digital infrastructure have helped developing countries enhance energy supply, improve information connectivity and expand digital economy applications. Industrial and trade collaboration can enable countries to integrate into regional and global value chains. Infrastructure development enhances long-term performance. Additionally, cooperation in public health and agricultural technology strengthens the ability to address health risks and improve livelihoods. China's public goods initiatives offer comprehensive frameworks for global development. The Global Development Initiative supports the UN 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development, while the Global Security Initiative promotes dialogue and consultation to address security challenges. The Global Civilization Initiative emphasizes respect for diverse cultures and international exchanges, and the Global Governance Initiative advocates for sovereign equality, international rule of law, multilateralism, and better representation for developing countries. These initiatives provide guiding principles and frameworks for discussion, with specific projects serving as vehicles, creating a mutually reinforcing dynamic. Resolution 2758 demonstrates that developing countries can enhance their role in international affairs by using multilateral mechanisms to express positions and coordinate demands. Today, through collective action, Global South nations can transform shared development concerns into consistent policy coordination and institutional participation. Developing countries leverage regional cooperation, South-South mechanisms, and multilateral platforms such as the UN, Group of 77 and BRICS to transform their development demands into policy proposals, facilitating policy exchanges, position coordination, and participation in global governance. China engages deeply in global development governance through a three-stage mechanism: expanding opportunities, building capacity, and fostering institutional participation. This approach enables developing countries to participate more broadly in global economic activities. By focusing on talent training, technology application, industrial ecosystems, and public governance capacity building, external cooperation can be effectively translated into local development outcomes. Ultimately, developing countries seek to enhance their international influence by proposing policies, participating in agenda setting, influencing rule discussions, and including legitimate concerns and stakeholders in international decision-making. On issues such as development financing, food security, climate change, and digital governance, strengthening South-South cooperation and multilateral coordination boosts their participation and encourages the international community to better address diverse development needs. As developing countries enhance their development capacity, they gain practical experience and expertise to engage more effectively in global governance discussions. Through regional cooperation, South-South mechanisms and multilateral platforms, they can strengthen information exchange, coordinate policy positions, and unify diverse development demands into common policy propositions. This synergy between development capacity and collective action forms a crucial foundation for the Global South to bolster its international influence. China's practice demonstrates that trade cooperation, infrastructure development, public health and food security support, knowledge sharing, and green and digital collaboration can enhance development foundations and create opportunities for developing countries by fostering self-reliance. Moving forward, it's crucial to align development needs with cooperation projects by integrating resources, technology, and talent support. Improving mechanisms for project implementation, operation, maintenance, and performance evaluation is essential. Promoting policy exchange and coordinating positions among developing countries through multilateral platforms will further these goals. Respecting the needs of countries, supporting their role as primary actors in cooperation, and enhancing local capacity building and sustainability of outcomes are also vital. Development-oriented practices, grounded in cooperation and supported by multilateral coordination, are expected to enhance the inclusiveness of global governance and boost the representation of developing countries. The author is the executive dean of the Country and Area Studies Academy at Beijing Foreign Studies University, dean of the BFSU-SOAS Joint Institute and a board member of the UN Association of China. item.title: Efforts urged for population development
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-24
Efforts urged for population development Meeting stresses aligning demographic dividend with broader social context Premier Li Qiang presided over an executive meeting of the State Council, China's Cabinet, on Friday with a key focus on coordinating population development and socioeconomic progress, as the country adapts to deepening demographic shifts. The meeting stressed that population is a fundamental factor in economic and social development, calling for better alignment between population and the broader economic, social, resource and environmental context — a policy vision in line with the 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-30), which emphasizes that high-quality population development underpins Chinese modernization. It called for further improvements to relevant policies and sustained efforts to build on and unlock China's comprehensive demographic dividend, so that high-quality population development can better support high-quality economic and social development. According to the National Bureau of Statistics, China's population stood at 1.4 billion at the end of 2025, a decrease of 3.39 million from the previous year. The population aged 60 and above reached 323 million, or 23 percent of the total, while the urbanization rate rose to 67.89 percent. The meeting stressed the need to place greater emphasis on all-around human development and improve people's scientific and cultural literacy, vocational skills, and physical and mental health. Efforts should be made to accelerate the establishment of a lifelong learning system for all, expand skills training, strengthen coordination between education, training and industrial development, and promote full and high-quality employment, it added. It also called for tailored guidance on population development across different regions, emphasizing orderly population movement between urban and rural areas, and steady progress toward equal access to basic public services. The meeting said that infrastructure planning should be optimized in light of population distribution, and that public service resources should be dynamically adjusted in response to changes in the resident population. It also underscored the need to accelerate the development of a birth-friendly society. Measures should be taken to continuously improve policies covering marriage, childbirth, child-rearing and education, and optimize fiscal, tax, social security and housing support for families, in a bid to stabilize the number of newborns, it added. Over the next five years, China will continue to refine its birth-support policies and vigorously promote high-quality population development, according to Lei Haichao, minister of the National Health Commission. Although annual births have declined in recent years, they still remain at a level of around 8 million, Lei said at a news conference last month, outlining the health sector's priorities for the 15th Five-Year Plan period. He said that very few countries maintain such a birth volume, which means China will still have abundant labor resources going forward.

item.title: Relief efforts intensify after Xizang quake kills 16, injures 76
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-24
President Xi Jinping has ordered all-out search and rescue efforts for the missing and prompt medical treatment for the injured after the earthquake. Sixteen people were killed and 76 others injured after the earthquake. Electricity and communications have been restored in some villages in the hardest-hit areas of Drachen county. Following the magnitude-7.0 earthquake in Drachen county, Nagqu, Xizang autonomous region, on Oct 22, many temporary housing units have been rushed in from Lhasa, with workers racing to complete their installation. A local Tibetan sweet-tea cafe is serving free hot meals to affected people. Rescue and relief operations continued on Saturday in Drachen county, Xizang autonomous region, as emergency workers and volunteers rushed to help residents affected by Thursday night's magnitude-7.0 earthquake. The quake, which struck at 10:33 pm on Thursday, has killed 16 people and injured 76 others, with 339 houses reported collapsed, according to a regional government. Authorities said on Friday that three rounds of searches had been completed, with no people reported missing. The regional government upgraded its emergency disaster relief response to Level II, effective Friday, to strengthen rescue operations and assistance to affected residents. In some of the hardest-hit villages in Maru township, rescue teams have been searching damaged buildings, setting up temporary shelters and delivering essential supplies. Volunteers have also joined the relief effort, offering food and other assistance to displaced residents. Sonam Ngodrub, who runs a Tibetan restaurant in Nagchu, traveled to one of the affected villages after the earthquake. "I run a Tibetan restaurant, and there isn't much else I can do apart from helping others," he said. "Every day, I can provide 100 to 150 kilograms of Tibetan noodles free of charge, along with roasted barley flour and sweet tea." Police officers and auxiliary personnel dug through rubble with their bare hands to rescue trapped residents in Drachen county, Xizang autonomous region, after a magnitude-7.0 earthquake struck at 10:33 pm on Thursday. A 45-member team from the county public security bureau set out at about 11 pm and traveled 85 kilometers, reaching the severely hit villages in Maru township at 12:30 am on Friday. "The only thing on our minds was getting the trapped residents out as quickly as possible," said Tsering Dawa, an officer with the county public security bureau. With temperatures dropping to minus 6 C and aftershocks continuing, 10 officers cleared fallen rocks from roads while the remaining 35 personnel searched for survivors in groups of three. They used drones to assess the damage, coordinated with village officials to check residents' whereabouts, and searched homes one by one. Before heavy machinery arrived, the rescuers used wooden poles to support unstable structures and squeezed through twisted door and window frames to reach trapped residents. They searched more than 200 households and helped transport injured people to hospital. After daybreak, the team directed traffic, transported supplies and set up more than 30 tents to shelter residents. BAQEN, Xizang - Sixteen people have been killed and 76 others are injured following a 7.0-magnitude earthquake that struck Baqen County of the city of Nagqu in southwest China's Xizang autonomous region at 10:33 pm on Thursday, local authorities said. The quake has also damaged or destroyed 339 homes and 20 livestock sheds, according to a press conference held on Friday afternoon by the information office of the Nagqu municipal government. Chinese President Xi Jinping has ordered all-out search and rescue efforts for the missing and prompt medical treatment for the injured, urging every effort to minimize casualties. Xi also called for close monitoring of seismic activity and weather conditions to prevent secondary disasters, as well as proper accommodation for affected residents and swift repairs to damaged infrastructure. Premier Li Qiang called for solid disaster prevention and response efforts, while the Ministry of Emergency Management (MEM) and authorities in Xizang have mobilized resources for rescue and relief operations. China has allocated 50 million yuan (about 7.5 million US dollars) in emergency disaster relief funds and earmarked another 30 million yuan for recovery efforts. The country has also upgraded its national earthquake emergency response from Level IV to Level III. More than 5,000 personnel have been deployed to the front lines of the disaster relief operation, working in teams responsible for search and rescue, medical treatment, temporary shelter and the provision of essential supplies. An emergency command headquarters has been established on the front lines to coordinate relief efforts. As of 10 a.m. Friday, 12,489 residents have been evacuated. After three rounds of comprehensive door-to-door checks, no missing persons had been reported as of 6 pm Friday, according to the emergency command headquarters. In a village of Maru Township, one of the hardest-hit areas near the epicenter, Xinhua reporters saw many houses completely collapsed, while others sustained extensive wall damage. Rows of emergency tents were erected in an open, safe area below the village. Half of villager Trinley's house collapsed, burying many of his belongings beneath the rubble. Two white tents were set up in his courtyard. "After the earthquake, our biggest concerns were where to stay and what to eat," Trinley said. "The government provided us with supplies including emergency tents, water and instant noodles," he added. The MEM said that on top of the 5,000 relief items previously allocated by the central government, an additional 5,000 central relief items, including tents, coats and folding beds were allocated. By coordinating efforts with other relief agencies and companies, the ministry said that it has also promptly allocated 43,000 other relief items, including mobile toilets, heating stoves, food and fuel, to ensure that affected people are properly resettled. The Red Cross Society of China has dispatched a working team to the disaster-hit area to guide local relief efforts. It has also allocated 3,800 sets of supplies, including family relief kits, hygiene kits, heaters, tents, jackets, folding beds and quilts. The society has additionally allocated 50 emergency toilet units to support affected residents and coordinated with the Chinese Red Cross Foundation to provide 500 family relief kits, 500 hygiene kits and more than 1,000 cartons of food to the quake-hit area. The China Charity Federation, one of the country's most influential charity organizations, has urgently allocated 3 million yuan to support emergency rescue endeavors. RESCUE CHALLENGES The earthquake zone has an average elevation of nearly 4,800 meters. The high-altitude, cold and low-oxygen environment, secondary disaster hazards and aftershock risks pose challenges to the relief efforts, local authorities said at the press conference. Deng Xiaogang, a rescuer with Nagqu's fire and rescue team, said that beyond the low temperatures and low oxygen levels, the biggest challenge was that the epicenter was in a pastoral area, where residents live far apart, making search-and-rescue operations more time-consuming in the initial stages. Some herding sites are up in the mountains, and the terrain is rugged, said Jigme Dorje, deputy head of the Baqen County public security bureau. "At first, machines could not reach these places, so we had to climb up and dig through the rubble with our hands, wearing only gloves," he said. Local authorities said that rescue teams will continue to take precautions to overcome difficulties in relief operations. Nighttime temperatures in the quake zone are low. Earthquake-triggered hazards such as landslides, collapses and falling rocks are currently the main secondary disaster risks. Earthquake monitoring, meteorological and emergency management departments, meanwhile, are coordinating closely to issue timely warnings of aftershocks and adverse weather conditions. Local authorities have launched round-the-clock intensified monitoring of key sites, including mountainsides, reservoirs, power stations, rivers, structurally unsafe buildings and telecommunications base stations. Emergency repairs are also underway, with damaged telecommunications and power facilities gradually being restored. Pan Zhiqing, Party secretary of Nagqu's emergency management bureau, said that in follow-up rescue work, personnel will be assigned to accompany rescue teams to inspect geological hazards along mountains and roads. Dangerous areas will be immediately cordoned off, and people and vehicles will be prohibited from passing. Transportation authorities will monitor road damage in real time, promptly repair and reopen blocked sections, and ensure smooth traffic flow. They will continue to coordinate with meteorological and natural resources departments and issue risk warnings, Pan added. China Telecom, China Mobile and China Unicom mobilized emergency repair teams, vehicles and equipment overnight, dispatching personnel to the quake-hit areas to restore communications services and inspect network facilities. All telecommunications base stations disrupted by the earthquake in Baqen County had been restored as of 10:30 a.m. Friday, according to the Xizang Communications Administration. The 7.0-magnitude earthquake was an extensional rupture, according to experts with the China Earthquake Networks Center (CENC). "An extensional fracture, in simple terms, occurs when the crust is stretched horizontally and, under tension and gravity, faultage slides downward along existing faultage, forming fractures and rupture surfaces," said Han Yanyan, a senior engineer with the earthquake prediction department of the CENC. President Xi Jinping has urged all-out search and rescue efforts for the missing and prompt medical treatment for the injured, in order to minimize casualties after a magnitude 7 earthquake rocked Drachen county in Nagchu, Southwest China's Xizang autonomous region. The quake, which struck at 10:33 pm on Thursday at a depth of 10 kilometers, killed 16 people, injured at least 76, and damaged or flattened 339 houses, with search for survivors continuing on Friday. In an instruction issued on Friday morning, Xi noted that the affected county is at a high altitude with low temperatures, emphasizing the need to closely monitor seismic activity and weather conditions to prevent secondary disasters. It is imperative to dispatch emergency rescue supplies, properly accommodate the affected residents, and repair damaged infrastructure as quickly as possible to safeguard people's lives and property, Xi said. In a separate instruction, Premier Li Qiang called for swift assessment of the situation. Given the county's high altitude and the frequent aftershocks, Li urged the Ministry of Emergency Management and the China Earthquake Administration, together with relevant authorities, to strengthen seismic monitoring and forecasting, and step up disaster prevention and response efforts. Surveillance footage shared by local media showed buildings shaking violently as the temblor struck, with goods falling off shelves and residents rushing outdoors. In Maru township, one of the hardest-hit areas in Drachen, the ground cracked open and sections of a road sank, China Central Television reported. China's national comprehensive fire and rescue force has dispatched 350 personnel and 83 vehicles to support operations in the quake-hit areas. The national earthquake emergency response was upgraded on Friday to Level III — the third highest in China's four-tier system — while a separate Level III national natural disaster relief response was also activated. The China Aerospace Science and Technology Corp has deployed satellites and unmanned aerial vehicles to aid rescue efforts. The corporation said it is coordinating resources at its disposal to facilitate emergency communication and support imaging of the quake-hit areas. The Ministry of Finance and the Ministry of Emergency Management have jointly allocated 50 million yuan ($7.5 million) to support rescue and relief operations, while the National Development and Reform Commission has earmarked an additional 30 million yuan from the central budget to help restore damaged infrastructure and public service facilities. The Red Cross Society of China has allocated 3,800 units of relief supplies, including hygiene kits, heating stoves and cotton tents, along with 50 sets of emergency toilets. On the ground, rescue teams have been working relentlessly. In Gangchen township, one of the areas closest to the epicenter, rescuers launched a door-to-door search in the early hours of Friday. In Maru, a resident trapped in a damaged house was rescued around 2:20 am by firefighters who arrived from Drachen. On Friday afternoon, Nagchu Mayor Dondrub said at an on-site news briefing that emergency relief supplies from central and local authorities were being promptly delivered to the affected county. He said that 18 temporary resettlement sites have been set up, providing displaced residents with warm shelter, food, clothing, clean drinking water and medical care. A total of 12,489 people have been relocated, he added. Power supply and communication networks are being restored gradually in the hardest-hit areas. All 628 mobile base stations, which were knocked offline by the earthquake, were restored by 10:30 am on Friday, according to the Xizang Communications Administration. Meng Linghe, Party chief of Drachen, said the quake-hit areas have an average elevation of nearly 4,800 meters, which means temperatures plummet after dusk. In addition to the freezing weather, the possibility of secondary disasters, such as landslides, poses grave risks, he said. As scattered snow showers are expected in the coming days, with ice and snow likely to cover high-altitude road sections, Meng urged rescue teams to remain alert and exercise caution when transporting personnel and supplies to the affected areas. Meanwhile, a magnitude 4.5 earthquake hit Zadoi county in neighboring Qinghai province at 10:14 pm on Friday, according to the China Earthquake Networks Center. The quake occurred at a depth of 10 km, with its epicenter located around 20 km from the epicenter of the Drachen temblor. Li Hongyang and Liu Boqian contributed to this story. BEIJING -- China has deployed satellites and unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) to aid rescue efforts following a 7.0-magnitude earthquake in Southwest China's Xizang autonomous region on Thursday evening. The China Aerospace Science and Technology Corporation (CASC) said on Friday that immediately after the disaster, it coordinated and deployed satellite resources to conduct emergency communication support and imaging of the quake-hit area. The CASC said it has activated multiple high-throughput satellite internet emergency service lines for the Ministry of Emergency Management, local emergency management authorities, and major telecom operators. Additional service line terminals are on their way to the quake-hit area. In response to satellite imaging requests for quake relief, the CASC immediately mobilized Gaofen-4 and other satellites to observe the quake-hit area. As of 7 am (Beijing Time) Friday, it had delivered four pre-disaster images and three post-disaster images, providing strong support for rescue and relief operations and disaster assessment. According to the Aviation Industry Corporation of China (AVIC), a UAV Wing Loong took off from an airport in Xigaze of Xizang autonomous region in the early hours of Friday and flew to the quake-hit area to carry out disaster observation and communication support missions. The AVIC said other Wing Loong teams are ready for deployment. Chinese People's Liberation Army Air Force also sent a UAV around midnight to the quake-hit area for disaster survey. Sixteen people were killed and 76 others injured after the earthquake struck Baqen county of Nagqu city in Xizang autonomous region at 10:33 pm Thursday, local authorities said on Friday. BEIJING -- The 7.0-magnitude earthquake that struck Baqen county of the city of Nagqu in Southwest China's Xizang autonomous region on Thursday was an extensional rupture, according to experts with the China Earthquake Networks Center (CENC). The quake occurred at around 10:33 pm, causing heavy casualties. Focal mechanism solutions show the event was basically consistent with regional tectonic characteristics. The CENC explained that the collision between the Indian and Eurasian plates had caused the uplift of the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau, crustal shortening and thickening, and widespread plateau deformation. These processes are the main dynamic mechanism controlling tectonic deformation in the western part of the Chinese mainland. The interior of the plateau is subjected to both north-south compression and east-west extension, and two typical fault systems, trending roughly north-south and east-west, have developed there. "The epicenter is located within the Changtang block of the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau, about 2 km from the nearest fault, the Baqen-Riwoqe fault," Han said. Under such intense crustal deformation, the Changtang block and its surrounding fault zones are particularly active. Since 1900, the block has experienced six earthquakes of magnitude 7 or above, including this one. The largest was a 7.5-magnitude earthquake in Shuanghu on Nov 8, 1997. "Therefore, this earthquake was an energy release of the Changtang block," Han said. Authorities in Nagchu city, Xizang autonomous region, warned at a Friday news conference that aftershocks and secondary disasters remain major risks following a magnitude-7.0 earthquake in Drachen county on Thursday night. The quake had killed 16 people and injured 76, said Dondrub, mayor of Nagchu. The affected area averages nearly 4,800 meters in elevation, according to Meng Linghe, Drachen's Party secretary. Landslides, slope collapses, and falling rocks are the main secondary geological hazards. Low nighttime temperatures, scattered snow showers, and black ice on shaded high-altitude roads pose risks to rescue vehicles. Dondrub said inspections have covered 12 roads spanning more than 1,700 kilometers, 201 bridges, and 324 culverts. Officials identified 11 hazards and cleared rockfalls at seven road locations. Earthquake, meteorological, and emergency management departments are consulting and issuing aftershock and weather warnings, while police and transport authorities keep emergency routes open. Round-the-clock monitoring and emergency repairs cover mountain slopes, reservoirs, power stations, river channels, unsafe buildings, and telecommunications base stations. Authorities are inspecting mountain slopes and roads alongside rescue teams, Meng said. Dangerous areas will be cordoned off, and search operations will be kept away from steep slopes. Authorities will inspect geological hazard sites and vulnerable infrastructure hourly and continue issuing updated risk alerts, Dondrub said. China's transport authorities have stepped up road inspections and emergency support to ensure rescue vehicles can reach areas affected by a magnitude-7.0 earthquake in Southwest China's Xizang autonomous region. Roads in the quake-hit area are under traffic controls, with access maintained for rescue vehicles while other vehicles are temporarily barred, according to the Ministry of Transport. The earthquake struck Drachen county in Nagchu at 10:33 pm on Thursday. By 10 am Friday, 16 people had been killed and 76 injured, according to local authorities. The ministry activated a Level III emergency response for road transport at 9 am Friday and dispatched a team to coordinate rescue support and efforts to keep roads open. It is also coordinating with the Ministry of Finance to arrange emergency funding for road clearance and repairs. Level III is the second-lowest level in the ministry's four-tier response system, with Level I being the highest. Xizang's transport department activated its own Level II response after the earthquake. Local highway authorities deployed 178 personnel and 39 pieces of machinery to inspect affected sections of five national highways and seven provincial roads. They have checked 2,377 kilometers of roads, 295 bridges and 635 culverts. The inspections found varying degrees of damage along sections of national highway G345 and provincial highway S301. More detailed inspections of roads, bridges and other transport infrastructure are continuing. Emergency equipment is being sent to the disaster-hit area from reserve centers in Lhasa and Qamdo to help crews clear debris and repair roads. Crews from nearby construction projects run by centrally administered State-owned enterprises, along with other road maintenance teams, are on standby to provide additional support. Electricity and communications have been restored in some villages in the hardest-hit areas of Drachen county, Xizang autonomous region, following a magnitude-7.0 earthquake on Thursday, according to the Xizang Communications Administration. State Grid Xizang Electric Power activated its emergency response and dispatched teams overnight to Gangche and Maru townships to inspect and secure power facilities. Electricity has been restored across the area surrounding the Maru township government offices. Phone and internet services have also returned to normal in two villages in the township. Being close to the earthquake's epicenter, they were among the most affected areas. According to the administration, the earthquake knocked 628 mobile base stations offline, accounting for 8.5 percent of the city's total. These stations have been restored as of 10:30 am Friday, bringing communications in the affected area back to pre-earthquake levels within 12 hours. The administration said 131 emergency repair personnel and 50 vehicles had been deployed to restore communications, along with 38 generators and other emergency equipment. Telecommunications networks in the disaster area are now operating normally, supporting the coordination of rescue operations. Earthquake authorities in Yunnan and Sichuan provinces have sent a dozen personnel to the affected area to assess the quake's intensity, verify damage, and conduct other emergency field operations. Sixteen people have been killed and 76 injured as of 1 pm Friday following Thursday's magnitude-7.0 earthquake in Drachen county, Xizang autonomous region, officials said at a news conference Friday. Dondrub, mayor of Nagchu city, which administers the county, said rescuers had completed three rounds of searches, checking key areas and visiting residents in remote, scattered settlements. Authorities have set up 18 temporary shelters and relocated 12,489 people, he said. Due to the quake, 339 households have collapsed or been damaged, along with 20 livestock sheds. The immediate priorities are treating the injured and ensuring displaced residents have access to basic necessities, he said. Authorities will provide insulated tents and hot meals, with particular attention to older people, children, pregnant women, new mothers, and people with disabilities. Rescuers went door to door in villages near the epicenter of a magnitude-7.0 earthquake that struck Drachen county, Xizang autonomous region, looking for anyone in need of help. In Gangche township, one of the areas closest to the epicenter, rescue workers began searching for people trapped in their homes in the early hours of Friday morning. Surveillance footage shared by local media showed buildings shaking violently, with goods tumbling from shelves as residents rushed outside to escape the quake on Thursday night. In Maru township, one of the hardest-hit areas, the earthquake cracked the ground and caused sections of road to sink, China Central Television reported. "Suddenly, there was a tremendous rumbling. For a moment, it felt as if hundreds of yaks were running at once," said Dzondru Tseltrim, a resident of Garuthang village in the county. His family had already gone to bed when the shaking began. Woken by the tremors, he heard cabinets and wooden pillars creaking inside the house. He rushed to wake his father, in his 80s, and helped him outside. Other family members soon followed. Fearing aftershocks, the family decided not to sleep indoors that night. They arranged for his father to rest in a car while the others prepared to spend the night in the courtyard. BEIJING -- China has allocated 50 million yuan (about $7.5 million) in emergency disaster relief funds and earmarked another 30 million yuan for recovery efforts following a 7.0-magnitude earthquake in Southwest China's Xizang autonomous region. The earthquake struck Drachen county of the city of Nagchu at 10:33 pm on Thursday, leaving 16 people dead and 65 injured. The Ministry of Finance and the Ministry of Emergency Management jointly allocated 50 million yuan to support rescue operations and assistance to affected residents, while the National Development and Reform Commission earmarked the additional 30 million yuan from the central budget to help restore damaged infrastructure and public service facilities. The country has also upgraded its national earthquake emergency response from Level IV to Level III, while activating a separate Level IV national natural disaster relief response. China's national comprehensive fire and rescue force has dispatched a total of 350 rescuers and 83 vehicles for rescue operations. The emergency management ministry has guided Xizang's emergency management department in arranging for Wing Loong drone deployment to the quake-hit area for disaster reconnaissance. As of 6:30 am on Friday, 120 rescuers and 27 vehicles had arrived in the quake-hit area, while the remaining 230 rescuers and 56 vehicles from the Xizang fire and rescue corps were en route as reinforcements, having all entered Nagqu's administrative area. Earlier, as of 4:30 am on Friday, authorities had mobilized relief supplies at the central, regional, municipal and county levels, and delivered them in batches to the affected area. These supplies included 1,000 prefabricated housing units, 3,239 tents, 2,821 folding beds and 4,280 quilts, among other essentials. The number of people injured in the 7.0-magnitude earthquake that struck Drachen county in Nagchu city, Xizang autonomous region, has risen to 65, including 11 seriously injured and 54 with minor injuries, according to the city's earthquake relief headquarters. As of 10 am Friday, rescue teams had safely evacuated 12,489 residents from affected areas. Search and rescue operations, damage assessments, and efforts to provide temporary shelter for displaced residents are ongoing. By early Friday, rescue teams and relief supplies reached earthquake-hit Drachen county in Nagchu, Xizang autonomous region, as authorities upgraded the national earthquake emergency response to Level III, the third highest of the four-tier system, the Ministry of Emergency Management said on Friday. A 7.0-magnitude earthquake struck the county at 10:33 pm on Thursday, killing 16 people and injuring 54. A working team from the central government has been dispatched to the disaster area to guide and assist relief efforts. The ministry has guided the Xizang autonomous region's emergency management department to send Wing Loong drones to the disaster area to assess the damage. By 4:30 am on Friday, relief supplies allocated by authorities at the central, autonomous region, city, and county levels had arrived in the disaster area. The relief supplies comprised of 1,000 prefabricated housing units, about 3,200 tents, about 2,800 folding beds, and 100 mattresses, along with quilts, stoves, cotton clothing, overcoats, and Tibetan robes. Also included were four generators, 1,000 hand-crank solar flashlights, and 1,000 head-mounted outdoor lights. By 6:30 am on Friday, 120 personnel and 27 vehicles had arrived in the disaster area. Another 230 personnel and 56 vehicles from the Xizang Fire and Rescue Corps were en route, having reached Nagchu. The Red Cross Society of China has activated an emergency response on Friday, allocating 3,800 sets of relief supplies, including hygiene kits, heating stoves, cotton tents, windproof jackets, folding beds, and cotton quilts. It has also dispatched a working group to the disaster zones to guide local efforts in relocating affected residents. China's Ministry of Natural Resources activated a Level III geological disaster emergency response for the Xizang autonomous region at 6 am on Friday, after a magnitude-7.0 earthquake struck the region on Thursday evening. According to the China Earthquake Networks Center, the quake hit Drachen county of Nagchu city in Xizang at 10:33 pm on Thursday, with a focal depth of 10 kilometers. So far, at the time of publication, it has resulted in 16 deaths and 54 injuries. Under the third-highest level emergency response in the four-tier system, an expert working group has been dispatched by the ministry to the quake-hit area to assist with emergency technical support, secondary geological hazard screening, and on-site disposal. The ministry required the Xizang natural resources department to carry out immediate patrols and investigations, strengthen monitoring and early warning, conduct joint risk assessments, handle disaster reports, and maintain 24-hour duty with timely information reporting. The China Geological Survey and the ministry's technical guidance center for geological disasters were tasked with coordinating expert deployments and enhancing assessment and scheduling to support local disaster prevention efforts. Rescue teams are continuing search and rescue operations on Friday after a 7.0-magnitude earthquake struck Drachen county in Nagchu city, Xizang autonomous region, killing 16 people and injuring 65 others. As of 10 am on Friday, 11 people were seriously injured and 54 sustained minor injuries, the city's earthquake relief headquarters said, Xinhua News Agency reported. A total of 339 households had homes collapsed or were damaged, while 20 livestock enclosures were damaged. The earthquake struck at 10:33 pm Thursday at a depth of 10 kilometers, according to the China Earthquake Networks Center. Firefighters rescued a trapped resident from a village at around 2:20 am Friday, CCTV reported. Rescue personnel were also conducting searches and damage assessments in other affected villages. Xizang's fire and rescue authorities mobilized 347 rescuers and 82 vehicles, along with more than 4,200 pieces of rescue equipment. More than 300 police officers were also dispatched to the hardest-hit areas, according to Xinhua. Emergency supplies dispatched by authorities at national, regional, municipal, and county levels began arriving in the disaster zone by 4:30 am, including 1,000 prefabricated housing units, 3,239 tents, 2,821 folding beds, 4,280 quilts, and winter clothing. Xizang has activated a Level III emergency response for disaster relief, while national authorities have upgraded their Level IV response to Level III and dispatched working groups to assist local rescue and relief operations. The Nagchu meteorological observatory warned that intermittent snow showers and strong winds could affect the earthquake-hit area over the next three days, with snow accumulation and icy roads posing additional risks to rescue and transport operations. A magnitude-7 earthquake struck Drachen county of Nagchu city, Xizang autonomous region at 10:33 pm on Thursday, with a focal depth of 10 kilometers, China Earthquake Networks Center reported. The county has a population of 56,200, official statistics showed.

item.title: Xi: Cooperation vital for global governance reform
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-24
Xi: Cooperation vital for global governance reform President Xi Jinping has called for joint efforts to implement the Global Governance Initiative and build a more just and equitable global governance system, as well as a better world, bringing greater certainty and positive energy to a world marked by turbulence and change. He made the remarks in a congratulatory letter sent on Friday to the 2026 Global Governance Forum (Xiong'an), which opened in the Xiong'an New Area, Hebei province, on the same day. In his message, Xi said that changes unseen in a century are accelerating across the world, while deficits in peace, development, security and governance continue to grow. China stands ready to work with all parties to uphold a vision of global governance featuring extensive consultation, joint contribution and shared benefits, strengthen confidence, pool strength and tackle challenges through cooperation, he said. Xi called for efforts to advance the initiative's implementation and move together toward a community with a shared future for humanity. Foreign Minister Wang Yi read out Xi's letter and delivered a keynote speech at the forum's opening ceremony. In his address, Wang announced a series of practical measures to advance global governance reform, including establishing a global governance research center to provide intellectual support for reform. Wang said that China will release a progress report on its AI Capacity-Building Action Plan for Good and for All. A position paper on strengthening outer space governance was released on Friday evening. Other measures include a training program on economic, social and cultural rights to support capacity building in developing countries and promote the full and effective implementation of the agreement on marine biodiversity beyond national jurisdiction, known as the BBNJ Agreement. Wang noted that the Global Governance Initiative has received support from more than 160 countries and international organizations, while over 60 countries have joined the Group of Friends of Global Governance. The GGI's core principles have been incorporated into documents of meetings of the Group of 20, the Shanghai Cooperation Organization and BRICS. Wang urged stronger collective action to implement the initiative, saying a multipolar world and greater democracy in international relations represent the direction of history. He called for upholding the United Nations' central role and revitalizing it through reform, ensuring all countries can participate in global governance and share its benefits equally. Major countries should uphold equality, honor commitments, stand for justice and pursue cooperation, he said. Wang urged a greater voice for the Global South, faster reform of the international financial system in line with agreed timetables, and increased representation for developing countries on the UN Security Council, prioritizing Africa's concerns. He also called for safeguarding the multilateral trading system centered on the World Trade Organization, promoting fair and open trade, and fully implementing the UN 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development. The deep sea, polar regions and outer space should be areas of cooperation rather than zero-sum competition, Wang said. He also urged an early, broadly agreed framework for artificial intelligence governance to keep the technology under human control and ensure it benefits the people. Guillaume Moumouni, a Beninese associate professor at the School of Foreign Languages of Northwest University in Xi'an, Shaanxi province, said that unilateralism and continuing conflicts underscore the need for multilateral cooperation, particularly in the Global South. China's approach emphasizes peace, respect for sovereignty, and seeking common ground while acknowledging differences, he said, adding that the nation plays an important role in representing the fundamental interests of the Global South.

item.title: Second phase of 140th Canton Fair opens in Guangzhou
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-23
Second phase of 140th Canton Fair opens in Guangzhou Share - WeChat
The second phase of the 140th session of the China Import and Export Fair, commonly known as the Canton Fair, opened on Friday in Guangzhou, Guangdong province, focusing on quality home living products. The massive exhibition features zones for household items, gifts and decorations, and building materials and furniture, according to the event's organizers. The fair aims to create an efficient global platform for the procurement of home living products.
